newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu believed still in Zaire - family friend.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu believed still in Zaire - family friend.

text.p: Zaire's ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko, earlier reported to have fled into exile in Morocco, was still in his home village of Gbadolite on Sunday morning, a friend of the family said.
The man, who asked not to be named, told Reuters he had been in touch by satellite telephone with Mobutu's family in Gbadolite at 10 a.m. (0800 GMT).
He said later attempts to speak to Gbadolite had failed but, even if he had left, Mobutu could not be in Morocco as the flight would take at least five hours.
"I am sure he is not in Morocco...The report was wrong," he said.

A Moroccan official earlier said Mobutu and his family had fled Zaire after Laurent Kabila's rebels overran the capital Kinshasa, and were staying at the Amphitrite hotel, some 20 km (12 miles) south of Rabat. He said they were expected to move later to the southern Moroccan city of Marrakesh.

The Mobutu family friend, who said he was in Paris, was contacted on a portable telephone used by close aides of Mobutu when the ousted president was recovering from cancer surgery at his French Riviera mansion in Roquebrune Cap Martin earlier this year.
He said he did not know what Mobutu's plans were. "Only he can decide," he said.
The spokesman in France of Kabila's rebels, Zamba Afri Kounyen, vowed to hunt Mobutu "wherever he goes" in exile.
"With us, he will never be in peace. Wherever he goes we will find him," he told radio France-Info in an interview.
"We know quite well where he will go," Kounyen added, warning France against giving shelter to Mobutu.
France backed Mobutu long after other western powers dropped him, but French officials say they are not aware of his plans.
Commentators say that Paris is unlikely to offer him shelter, at least before the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election for fear that his presence would be a campaign issue.
